Same apple. Only one half goes brown.
Would you still eat it?
Same apple,
same cut.
So why is only one half
going brown?
It isn't rot.
The apple is doing
it to itself.
Cutting bursts its cells.
An enzyme spills out
onto the fruit's own
polyphenols.
Add oxygen,
and it turns them into
quinones that clump into
brown pigment.
The white half got lemon juice.
Acid slows the enzyme,
and vitamin C undoes
its first step.
